items.title: Goodbye October, Hello Movember!
items.author: Charlotte Cochrane
items.excerpt: With Halloween in the rearview mirror, Movember is officially upon us! Bishop’s University’s men’s rugby team is participating in this month-long event which raises funds for men’s health initiatives. The Movember website states that they’ve raised over
items.leadExcerpt: With Halloween in the rearview mirror, Movember is officially upon us! Bishop’s University’s men’s rugby team is participating in this month-long event which raises funds for men’s health initiatives. The Movember website states that they’ve raised over “$1.8 billion AUD in prevention-focused work across mental health and suicide prevention, prostate cancer and testicular cancer”, in the past 22 years, worldwide. Movember is the type of fundraiser that not only brings community and funds research, but also raises awareness regarding men’s health– something that is not nearly talked about enough.

The City of Sherbrooke certainly does, and it is going to reduce the number of available on-street parking spaces in Lennoxville even more. Sherbrooke is planning to uniformize parking restrictions on Queen St., Speid St., Church St. and Samuel-Gratham St. While both Queen St. and Speid St. offer free, unrestricted parking spaces in Lennoxville, Church St. and Samuel-Gratham St. have restrictions ranging from 60 to 120 minutes.

items.title: Community Cupboard Sees Increase in Demand as Food Insecurity Persists
items.author: Florence Robert
items.excerpt: As the cost of living continues to rise, access to affordable groceries has become an increasing struggle for post-secondary students. Between having to pay for rent, tuition, groceries and other living expenses, students are often left choosing between basic
items.leadExcerpt: As the cost of living continues to rise, access to affordable groceries has become an increasing struggle for post-secondary students. Between having to pay for rent, tuition, groceries and other living expenses, students are often left choosing between basic needs and the heavy demands of university life. A February 2025 survey conducted by Équiterre, a non-profit environmental organization, found that 44 per cent of students across six Quebec colleges experienced some form of food insecurity. The high prices of groceries are not the only problem. Limited time between classes and work, lack of cooking equipment and stigmas surrounding financial insecurity all contribute to food insecurity.

items.title: Too Successful or Forgotten? Many Menstrual Product Boxes Empty on Campus
items.author: Charlotte Cochrane
items.excerpt: The menstrual product boxes have consistently been empty in many of the bathrooms across campus since the beginning of the semester. The Menstrual Equity Project team has been inquiring with the Student Representative Council (SRC) and the custodial staff
items.leadExcerpt: The menstrual product boxes have consistently been empty in many of the bathrooms across campus since the beginning of the semester. The Menstrual Equity Project team has been inquiring with the Student Representative Council (SRC) and the custodial staff on campus to try and find an explanation and solution to this issue. The empty menstrual product boxes may be a result of students taking more than one “emergency” product at a time (i.e. stocking up on their products), says Erin Mallory, executive director of the SRC, in an email statement. The custodial staff have been asked to keep a closer eye on these boxes and to ensure that they are filled more frequently.

items.imageCredit: Photo : JasonParis / CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons
items.leadExcerpt: 25 years in the making! Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026 saw the Gaiters Women’s Soccer team break a long-lasting streak of missing the playoffs. The 25-year curse, if you may, has been broken in a new era under the reign of Head Coach Fawn Mulholland. In only her second year as the manager of the team, Mulholland, alongside her staff, led the Gaiters to a 6-6-2 regular season record, seeing them finish fourth in the RSEQ. It was not an easy pathway to clinching a playoff spot. The Gaiters were in a race to the finish line as they dropped valuable points around the midseason mark, leaving their fate in their own hands with three games to go. Bishops went on to win their final three games of the year, permitting them to gain a playoff spot.

items.excerpt: Sur YouTube, dans les balados ou à la télévision, les affaires criminelles sont devenues des récits à consommer. Néanmoins, derrière chaque histoire d'un crime se trouvent des victimes, des proches et des événements bien réels. Entre intérêt du public, divertissement et respect
items.leadExcerpt: Sur YouTube, dans les balados ou à la télévision, les affaires criminelles sont devenues des récits à consommer. Néanmoins, derrière chaque histoire d’un crime se trouvent des victimes, des proches et des événements bien réels. Entre intérêt du public, divertissement et respect des personnes concernées, où placer la limite ? Raconter une affaire criminelle implique des choix : quelles informations retenir, quelles images montrer et quels détails laisser de côté. Pour la journaliste de faits divers à La Presse Mayssa Ferah, le premier critère reste l’intérêt public. « Tout ce qui aide les gens à comprendre pourquoi c’est arrivé » peut ainsi être pertinent, selon elle.

items.title: Larger Than Life: Short King Warsame
items.author: Isabelle Lim
items.excerpt: In a video that has now amassed over 5,000 views on Instagram, Short King Warsame poses in front of an elevator in a bright, patterned yellow polo shirt and black slacks. One hand in his pocket, he smiles bashfully for the camera, flashing a cheeky thumbs up. The caption reads,
items.leadExcerpt: Image courtesy of Warsame Ahmed In a video that has now amassed over 5,000 views on Instagram, Short King Warsame poses in front of an elevator in a bright, patterned yellow polo shirt and black slacks. One hand in his pocket, he smiles bashfully for the camera, flashing a cheeky thumbs up. The caption reads, “3’9” with 6’ confidence” — which, in just a few words, sums up Warsame’s ethos. Many members of the McGill community know Short King Warsame from their Instagram Reels feeds. With thousands of views on each reel and just over 2,000 followers at the time of writing (though he’s aiming for 10,000 by the end of 2026), Warsame is well-known both on and off campus as a beacon of positivity on social media. His most popular posts feature light-hearted content, mostly football commentary and videos of him at house parties and social events like OAP. In each post, he wears his signature toothy smile; except, of course, in the videos where he’s lamenting his woes as a fan of Manchester United.

items.imageCredit: Photo : Jean Gagnon / CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
items.leadExcerpt: McGill University encourages its students to think critically, question authority, and engage with the political issues that shape the world around them. Its own teaching guidelines emphasize questioning assumptions and examining competing perspectives, while its Statement of Academic Freedom recognizes the right to criticize university policies and administration. However, when students turn that same critical attention toward McGill’s own decisions, the university’s commitment to open debate becomes more complicated.

items.leadExcerpt: Any artist’s willingness to share the custody of their music must not be taken as a sign of it being impersonal. “It’s not mine, it’s ours,” Kline tells Radio TinTin, reflecting on releasing her music to the public. Kline has made a career out of confessional songwriting, creating lyrical and musical projects that are diary-like in tone — a diary that was never meant to reach millions of people. Reaching millions of people is exactly what happened, however, when her 2016 song “Fool” went viral on TikTok in early 2021. It has now appeared in 367 thousand total videos on the platform, and counts over 220 million streams on Spotify.

items.title: “It’s Our Livelihood”: AMUSE Pushes for Job Security at McGill
items.author: Lorin Kamaci
items.excerpt: The Association of McGill University Support Employees (AMUSE) is pushing for more consistent rules on discipline, scheduling, and paid hours, saying casual employees face varying practices across McGill departments. These concerns form part of its ongoing negotiations with the
items.leadExcerpt: Courtesy of AMUSE The Association of McGill University Support Employees (AMUSE) is pushing for more consistent rules on discipline, scheduling, and paid hours, saying casual employees face varying practices across McGill departments. These concerns form part of its ongoing negotiations with the university, which most recently met with the union on October 5 to discuss disciplinary procedures, probation, and hiring practices, with several issues remaining unresolved. According to its bargaining team, AMUSE represents approximately 1,300 to 1,600 casual employees, employees hired on a temporary or occasional basis, at McGill. Its collective agreement expired on May 31, 2025. The union developed its bargaining strategy through member surveys conducted in 2024 and 2025, as well as a special general meeting in September 2025.

items.leadExcerpt: L’Entracte is both a successor in this lineage of student-run venues, and a registered nonprofit. “All of the [proceeds are] distributed to musicians, to artists, to making a better venue,” said Dumouchel. While employees have standard wages, the leadership team works on a volunteer basis. “Since this is a nonprofit, community is everything,” Dumouchel added. The Daily spoke with Kevin Dean, a longtime McGill professor and staple within the Montreal jazz scene. “[L’Entracte] is a very ambitious project, butit has great potential and they seem to be on the right track.” Dean, who has lent his Hammond B3 organ and piano to the venue, says he’s keen to help out where he can. “It would be nice to have three full-time jazz clubs in town.” A virtuosic trumpet player and band leader in his own right, Dean runs a Sunday organ night at the venue twice a month, and regularly collaborates with student musicians.
